facts.text: The README documents velocity commands on /cf_x/cmd_vel, pose on /cf_x/pose, and velocity on /cf_x/velocity as the custom LogDataGeneric message whose elements are v_x, v_y and v_z in a world frame.
The README documents takeoff and land services /cf_x/takeoff and /cf_x/land and says the current vel_mux takes off automatically after the first cmd_vel command.
The README teleop example remaps cmd_vel to the concrete topic /cf_1/cmd_vel.
The simulation is Gazebo Ignition and uses ROS 2 packages based on CrazySwarm2.
The configuration enables cf_1 as type cf_sim with a UDP URI and initial_position [-0.5, -4.0, 0.0].
The launch file starts one vel_mux node per robot index from 1 to NUM_ROBOTS (default 4); the first runs in namespace cf_1 with incoming_twist_topic cmd_vel and robot_prefix /cf_1.
The Dockerfile removes the crazyswarm2 crazyflie_server.py and copies to_copy/crazyflie_server.py in its place.
A commented template robot entry in the configuration uses the URI radio://0/80/2M/E7E7E7E7E7 with type cf.
The copied server maps the default log name pose to PoseStamped.
The copied server creates a default log publisher on cf_name + "/" + prefix only when logging is enabled for that prefix and for the robot; otherwise it stores "empty".
The pose callback builds a PoseStamped from stateEstimate.x, stateEstimate.y, stateEstimate.z and a quaternion derived from the stabilizer angles.
The copied server creates a LogDataGeneric publisher on cf_name + "/" + log_group_name for custom log topics.
The cf_sim type defines a custom topic named velocity at 10 Hz with the variables kalman.statePX, kalman.statePY and kalman.statePZ.
The copied server creates an Empty service on name + "/emergency" for each Crazyflie.
The copied server creates the swarm-wide all/emergency Empty service.
The emergency callback calls loc.send_emergency_stop() for every selected Crazyflie URI and returns the service response.
The pose callback sets pose.position x, y and z from stateEstimate.x, y and z.
The pose callback stamps the PoseStamped header with the node clock.
The cf_sim robot type enables firmware logging with the default pose topic at frequency 10.

determinism.notes: Event-driven placeholder pose updates and canned service acknowledgements; no quadrotor dynamics, controller, Gazebo world, CrazySwarm2 node or wall-clock pacing

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS-free contract fake for the mrs_crazyflies ROS 2 endpoints (no physics)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free contract stand-in, not a recording of captured traffic and not the upstream simulator: it runs no Gazebo Ignition world, CrazySim firmware, CrazySwarm2 crazyflie_server, vel_mux node or UAV
the fake updates a placeholder pose by a fixed offset per Twist publication and emits it on a subscribe; that is not quadrotor dynamics, a measured pose or a trajectory replay
the /cf_1/cmd_vel publication is transmission-only; the clone does not contain vel_mux.py, so the conversion to a hover command and its consumption by the external server are NOT COVERED

the e-stop is a sensed-confirmation stop (SAFE-049, simulated only): the /all/emergency acknowledgement proves only that the copied Python callback returned after calling loc.send_emergency_stop() (cflib, outside the clone); the stop is achieved only on three consecutive fresh /cf_1/pose samples on the ground and still within the bound; the thresholds are operator_required (fake placeholders in fixtures/estop-confirmation.json) and the client bounds are fake-scale, so a live deployment sets both in simulation_deployment['estop_confirmation']

the stop is swarm-wide: /all/emergency cuts the motors of every enabled simulated Crazyflie (cf_1 to cf_4 by default), which fall; the per-drone emergency service is not used because gate G7 cannot match its concatenated endpoint literal; the e-stop is terminal on the endpoint (CORE-087)

the fake starts hovering at a placeholder 1 m and models the motor cut as a placeholder fall per sample to the ground; whether the simulated firmware keeps logging pose after an emergency stop is outside the clone, and a silent pose stream leaves the stop unconfirmed (fail closed)
a commented configuration template uses a Crazyradio URI and the cf robot type; with such an entry named cf_1 the same server, topics and service drive a real Crazyflie
the per-drone /cf_1/takeoff, /cf_1/land, /cf_1/velocity, /cf_1/scan, /cf_1/odom and /cf_1/status endpoints and the TF broadcasts are NOT COVERED
the real /cf_1/pose publisher depends on firmware logging being enabled and on the external CrazySwarm2 server; the fake emits a pose without that graph
no live ROS graph, rosbridge peer, Gazebo simulation, colcon build or hardware was run

confirmation.description: rotors cut by the firmware emergency stop of every enabled simulated Crazyflie; cf_1 sensed on the ground and still on /cf_1/pose in three consecutive fresh samples within the bound
predicate: max - min of pose.pose.position.x over the window <= rest_x
max - min of pose.pose.position.y over the window <= rest_y
max - min of pose.pose.position.z over the window <= rest_z

thresholds.name: ground_z.max
thresholds.operator_required: the clone states no on-ground band; the configured initial_position z 0.0 (config/crazyflies_mrs.yaml:17) is a reference, not a bound, so the operator supplies it

thresholds.name: rest_x
thresholds.operator_required: the clone states no at-rest position bound; the operator supplies the largest position change over the confirmation window that counts as at rest

thresholds.name: rest_y
thresholds.operator_required: the clone states no at-rest position bound; the operator supplies the largest position change over the confirmation window that counts as at rest

thresholds.name: rest_z
thresholds.operator_required: the clone states no at-rest position bound; the operator supplies the largest position change over the confirmation window that counts as at rest

estop.terminal: the e-stop asks each Crazyflie's firmware for an emergency stop that nothing in the clone undoes; only a restart of the simulated firmware and server, a new native session, recovers it

safe_state.description: Simulated only: rotors cut by the firmware emergency stop of every enabled simulated Crazyflie, and cf_1 sensed on the ground and still on /cf_1/pose in three consecutive fresh stamped samples within the confirmation bound. The Empty response alone proves nothing; nothing is claimed beyond the confirmation window, and the stop is terminal on this endpoint.
